title: Introduce sampled prefetch tracing and delta-token-latency heatmap
author: Anika Bose
description:
Motivation: We see recurring long-tail latency spikes where downstream token generation spends extra time in prefetch/KV-prefill and late-arriving cache hydrations. Existing token-level metrics attribute cost but do not separate time spent in prefetch vs token emission, which makes root-cause for tail latency noisy and increases paging for on-call.

What this PR does: Adds a lightweight, sampled prefetch tracing layer + a token-delta-latency metric and Grafana heatmap to visualize per-token delta (time between token request and token emission) broken down by prefetch/hydration phases. The tracing hooks are sampled (configurable) and add low-cardinality tags; metric rollups are aggregated server-side and exposed in existing metric export pipelines. Also introduces alert tuning based on the 95/99 delta-latency rollups to reduce noisy incidents.

Changes included (high level): commits listed below; key files changed listed under changed_files. Implementation choices: sampling is controlled by feature-flag and rate-limited per-tenant to avoid PII/high-cardinality. We hash the prefetch-key to a 16-bit bucket to provide distribution visibility without raw keys. Heatmap panels are prepared as a JSON dashboard that can be imported into Grafana.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag (runtime.prefetch_tracing.enabled) and a per-tenant rate cap. Default: off for all tenants; rollout plan: internal dogfood -> beta tenants -> global. No breaking API changes.

Testing and validation: unit tests for collector and hash-bucketing added; an integration test simulates KV late-arrival and asserts delta attribution and metrics emitted. Load-tested in perf lab at 2x baseline QPS with sampling enabled to verify <1% CPU overhead in the runtime trace path.

Follow-ups (future work): integrate heatmap with token-cost attribution view, add span-level correlation to user-facing request IDs for easier drill-down, and add a compact aggregation for long-term retention.

Checklist:
- [x] Add sampled tracing hooks and span enrichment
- [x] Emit token-delta-latency metric and rollup labels
- [x] Add Grafana heatmap and dashboard JSON
- [x] Documentation page and rollout notes
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Feature-flag and tenant rate limiting

review_comments:
Samir Patel (2026-02-16): This is great direction. Concern: are we introducing a new high-cardinality tag (prefetch_key)? Please confirm hashing and cardinality limits.
Author reply (Anika): We hash to a 16-bit bucket and rate-limit per-tenant. The raw key is never exported. Added tests to assert bucket distribution.

Marta Ruiz (2026-02-18): Can we expose the sampling rate metric so we can reason about observability coverage? Also add a Grafana panel for sampling rate.
Author reply (Anika): Added runtime.prefetch_tracing.sample_rate metric and included a small panel in the dashboard JSON (commit f9c3b22).

Ethan Cole (2026-02-20): Tests look good, but please add an integration test that simulates late KV hydration causing >50ms token delta.
Author reply (Anika): Added integration test that asserts metric rollup and trace presence (test/integration/prefetch_tracing_test.go). CI initially failed on lint; fixed import ordering and updated docs formatting.
release_notes: Adds sampled prefetch tracing and token-delta-latency heatmap for better attribution of long-tail latency; feature-gated and rollout controlled; includes alert smoothing to reduce noisy delta-latency incidents.
